newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Friday.

"There were few sell-offs in the market today but only on a small scale. The market has freezed off securities because the local money trend is towards the Thai market. The hike in the interbank rate had only slight impact, we will see on Monday whether there will be any MAS intervention," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.89/2.84 percent from Thursday's yield of 2.80/2.75 percent and one-year at a yield at 2.82/2.77 percent against 2.83/2.78 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.45/98.50 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.55/98.60, September 2001 at S$96.25/96.35 against S$96.30/96.40 and June 2003 at S$94.03/94.08 from S$94.15/94.20.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 4-1/2 4-3/8
